# Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing — facts

> Source-anchored units about Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing: 8 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 8 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Atlas's documented default deployment is a replica set with at least three database instances. The tier specifies resources available to each node; the tier's RAM is not a single pool shared by the entire replica set. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/high-availability.md · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing · also: https://archtenet.dev/blog/mongodb-geosharding-hidden-cost/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB's billing documentation directs users to the overall Cluster Overview charges and warns that the creation-time tier cost for a multi-region cluster is based only on its preferred region. Its pricing calculator accepts provider, region and instance configuration and says estimates can differ from actual charges. A configured total is a stronger comparison basis than an unqualified starting price. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/pricing/calculator

## Facts and statements

- [statement] ArchTenet's August 3, 2026 engineering account explicitly interprets Atlas's quoted dedicated-cluster rates as covering a standard three-node replica set; Flexera's comparison also says its listed cluster prices include three nodes. This supports an included-replica interpretation of those quotes, but does not establish that arbitrary extra replicas are included. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://archtenet.dev/blog/mongodb-geosharding-hidden-cost/ · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing · also: https://www.flexera.com/blog/finops/snowflake-vs-mongodb/
- [statement] MongoDB's Atlas Core billing documentation explicitly charges cluster and storage costs for each data-bearing node. It defines the node count as the replication factor for a replica set, or replication factor times shard count for a sharded cluster. An included-replica cluster quote therefore must not be interpreted as node-independent billing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing
- [statement] EC2 On-Demand pricing explicitly meters each launched instance until it stops or terminates. For three identical continuously running instances, compute cost is three times one instance's runtime charge; this is an arithmetic consequence of EC2's per-instance meter, not evidence that an Atlas cluster quote should also be multiplied by three. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/ · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing
- [statement] For an HA cost comparison, first determine whether each quoted rate is per node or for the configured replica set. Multiply per-node rates by node count and runtime, but do not multiply an already complete replica-set total again. This is a comparison method inferred from Atlas's node-based billing documentation, the engineering account's cluster-price interpretation, and EC2's explicit per-instance meter. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing · also: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/, https://archtenet.dev/blog/mongodb-geosharding-hidden-cost/
- [statement] Adding shards or increasing replication changes the billable topology. MongoDB's billing formula counts replication factor times shard count, and ArchTenet's field account describes a tier-cost increase recurring per shard. Standard-set pricing does not remove the economic multiplier from additional shards. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs/ · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing · also: https://archtenet.dev/blog/mongodb-geosharding-hidden-cost/
- [statement] Credex's August 14, 2026 guide multiplies the advertised M10 rate of $0.08/hour by three nodes and 730 hours to reach $175.20/month. ArchTenet instead says roughly $0.08/hour covers the entire three-node set. The arithmetic is internally consistent but the assumed price unit conflicts; do not use the Credex total as an independently verified Atlas HA price. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://credex.rocks/blog/buy-mongodb-credits-at-up-to-50-percent-off-how-to-fix-an-atlas-bill-that-tripled-overnight · keywords: Atlas included-replica pricing vs per-instance HA billing · also: https://archtenet.dev/blog/mongodb-geosharding-hidden-cost/
